interest: This document illustrates the State Department's recordkeeping practices regarding diplomatic etiquette and ceremonial courtesies extended to foreign heads of state during the interwar era. It highlights the use of radio broadcasting in 1931 by Secretary of State Henry L. Stimson to publicly convey birthday felicitations to Emperor Hirohito, reflecting bilateral diplomatic goodwill just months before the Mukden Incident of September 1931 led to escalating tensions between the two nations.
overview: This file consists of a single Department of State 'List of Papers' docket sheet (Form DS-46) for decimal file 894.458, concerning ceremonial communications and etiquette involving Japan. The sheet indexes a single entry dated April 27, 1931, referencing a radio address delivered by Secretary of State Henry L. Stimson extending birthday greetings to the Emperor of Japan (Hirohito), with a cross-reference directing researchers to decimal file 894.001 H 61/53a for Telegram No. 68 to Japan.

subfiles.about: A Department of State List of Papers docket sheet indexing an April 1931 radio broadcast by Secretary Stimson extending birthday greetings to the Emperor of Japan.
subfiles.summary: This Department of State List of Papers (Form DS-46) indexes records under classification 894.458 for ceremonial communications involving Japan. It notes document number 5 dated April 27, 1931, which contains the text of a radio speech by Secretary of State Henry L. Stimson wishing the Emperor of Japan a happy birthday. A notation directs the reader to decimal file 894.001 H 61/53a for related Telegram No. 68 sent to Japan.
